fake.h: Trainee pilot lands a glider on a supermarket roof in {} and shops before taking off again
fake.tell: A glider can't take off again on its own; it needs a winch or a tow plane.

fake.h: Fire crew in {} called to a blaze that turns out to be 214 candles on a single birthday cake
fake.tell: Nobody turns 214; that many candles makes no sense on a birthday cake.

fake.h: Family cat in {} is listed as head of household on a census return, and the form is accepted
fake.tell: Census forms are checked; a cat can't be accepted as head of household.

fake.h: Customs officers in {} seize 3,180 rubber ducks hidden inside a shipment of bathtubs
fake.tell: Rubber ducks aren't banned or taxed heavily, so there is no reason to smuggle them.

fake.h: Lighthouse keeper in {} repaints the tower in 7 colours after misreading a paint order
fake.tell: A lighthouse's colours are set by the maritime authority, not chosen by its keeper.

fake.h: Vending machine in {} drops 1,267 free chocolate bars after a moth lands on the service switch
fake.tell: A moth is far too light to trip a switch, and the service switch sits inside the locked machine.

fake.h: Postman in {} delivers 1,486 letters to one house after a child's drawing covers a street sign
fake.tell: Post is sorted by postcode and address, not by reading street signs.

fake.h: Stray llama spends 6 nights in a hotel lobby in {} before staff realise it is not a decoration
fake.tell: A live llama eats, moves and smells; staff would notice within minutes.

fake.h: Fishing trawler off {} nets a sunken piano that still plays 3 notes in tune
fake.tell: Seawater ruins a piano's strings and felts; nothing would still be in tune.

fake.h: Hiker in {} reports a UFO that turns out to be his own drone, still filming him 214 metres up
fake.tell: Drones run out of battery in about half an hour, so his own drone couldn't still be hovering over him.

fake.h: Hotel in {} bills a guest for 37 minibar items he drank while away on a 9-day cruise
fake.tell: He couldn't drink from the minibar while he was away at sea.

fake.h: Brass band plays the national anthem 27 times at a match in {} after the scoreboard jams
fake.tell: Anthems are played once before kick-off; a jammed scoreboard has nothing to do with them.

fake.h: Bin lorry in {} tips a parked hatchback into its hopper; the owner is charged a bulky-waste fee
fake.tell: A bin lorry's lift arms are built for wheelie bins; they can't lift a car.

fake.h: Booking slip sends 37 tour coaches to a farm track instead of the castle in {} in one morning
fake.tell: One booking error might misroute a coach, not 37 in one morning.

fake.h: Funicular in {} carries a sleeping passenger up and down 41 times before anyone wakes him
fake.tell: Funiculars are emptied at the terminus on every run.

fake.h: Pub quiz team in {} wins 63 weeks running before it turns out to be the quizmaster's 4 brothers
fake.tell: A local pub quiz would spot the quizmaster's brothers long before week 63.

fake.h: Orchestra in {} plays a whole symphony in total darkness after a power cut, finishing early
fake.tell: Musicians read their parts from the page; in total darkness they couldn't.

fake.h: Hospital in {} discharges a man after 6 days, then learns he was a visitor in a spare bed
fake.tell: Patients are registered on admission; a visitor wouldn't be fed and checked on for 6 days.

fake.h: Scarecrow in {} gets a parking ticket after a farmer leaves it driving his tractor in a field
fake.tell: Wardens don't ticket farm vehicles parked in fields.

fake.h: Fireworks in {} go off 4 hours early when a technician's phone alarm triggers the launch
fake.tell: Displays are fired from a control panel; a phone alarm can't launch them.

fake.h: Stolen garden bench in {} is returned with 214 new memorial plaques screwed along its back
fake.tell: A bench back has room for a few plaques, not 214.

fake.h: Herd of 41 goats sleeps across a bank's front steps in {}, delaying opening by 37 minutes
fake.tell: Staff use a back entrance; goats on the steps wouldn't keep a bank shut.

fake.h: Wind turbine in {} spins backwards for an afternoon and sends power to 9 homes the wrong way
fake.tell: Household electricity has no 'wrong way' for power to flow.

fake.h: Escaped emu joins a cycling time trial in {} and is given an official finishing time of 41:07
fake.tell: Race officials time registered riders, not animals that wander onto the course.

fake.h: Cheese wheel rolls 2.3 km downhill from a farm in {} and stops at the door of a rival dairy
fake.tell: A rolling cheese stopping at a rival's door is too neat a coincidence.

fake.h: Swans in {} block a motorway slip road for 41 minutes to escort 9 cygnets to a petrol station
fake.tell: Swans head for water, not petrol stations.

fake.h: Snow plough in {} clears 14 km of the wrong motorway after its satnav picks a ferry route
fake.tell: Ploughs follow assigned routes, and a ferry route can't put him on a motorway.

fake.h: Town clock in {} runs 13 minutes fast for 47 years until a schoolboy checks it on his phone
fake.tell: Phones weren't around to check a clock 47 years ago, so nobody could have missed it for that long.

fake.h: Escalator in {} runs backwards all day; shoppers climb it 8,417 times before staff notice
fake.tell: Staff and sensors would notice a backwards escalator in minutes, not after thousands of trips.

fake.h: Drawbridge in {} stays raised for 7 hours after the operator's lunch box jams the control lever
fake.tell: Drawbridges have manual overrides; a lunch box wouldn't keep one up for 7 hours.

fake.h: Pensioner in {} wins a village marrow contest with a cucumber, and the judges keep the result
fake.tell: A cucumber and a marrow look different enough that judges would spot it at once.

fake.h: Window cleaner in {} finishes a 37-storey tower in one afternoon on a single bucket of water
fake.tell: One bucket of water couldn't clean the windows of a 37-storey tower.

fake.h: Dealer in {} sells a ballpoint pen 'signed by Napoleon' to a retired dentist for 4,310 euros
fake.tell: Napoleon died in 1821; ballpoint pens weren't invented until the late 1930s.

fake.h: Smuggler in {} is caught with 3.4 kilos of caviar from male sturgeon hidden in a cello case
fake.tell: Caviar is roe, so it can only come from female sturgeon.

fake.h: Shoplifter, 34, in {} admits stealing 1,213 tuna tins over 33 years, hidden in a trombone case
fake.tell: A 34-year-old who has stolen for 33 years began at age one.

fake.h: Promoter in {} sells 642 tickets to watch a total solar eclipse at midnight from a rooftop
fake.tell: A solar eclipse needs the Sun in the sky, so it cannot happen at midnight.

fake.h: Collector in {} pays 7,300 euros for a 1979 laptop still running its original Windows 95
fake.tell: Windows 95 arrived sixteen years after 1979, and laptops barely existed then.

fake.h: Bakery in {} sells 'gluten-free' baguettes made from wheat for 9 weeks before anyone notices
fake.tell: Wheat flour contains gluten, so a wheat baguette can't be gluten-free.

fake.h: Burglar in {} who stole 48 organ pipes says he was at a wedding on 29 February 2023
fake.tell: 2023 was not a leap year, so there was no 29 February.

fake.h: Rider in {} says he cycled 383 km in 54 minutes to deliver a still-warm pizza
fake.tell: That would mean about 425 km/h, far beyond any cyclist.

fake.h: Burglar in {} is caught after posting footage of his break-in from an iPhone stolen in 2005
fake.tell: The first iPhone wasn't released until 2007, so none could be stolen in 2005.

fake.h: Metal detectorist, 67, in {} digs up a Roman coin stamped AD 140 under his potato patch
fake.tell: The AD dating system was devised centuries after Roman times, so no coin could carry it.

fake.h: Funeral director in {} says a client's fingernails grew 9 cm in the casket after death
fake.tell: Nails and hair don't keep growing after death; the skin just retracts.

fake.h: Cyclist, 36, in {} rides 1,350 km to his wedding in 9 hours, towing a sofa as a gift
fake.tell: 1,350 km in 9 hours is an average of 150 km/h, impossible on a bicycle.

fake.h: Auction buyer, 63, in {} pays €8,350 for a menu from the Titanic's last dinner, dated 1921
fake.tell: The Titanic sank in 1912, so a menu from its last dinner can't be dated 1921.
